summary.headline: Ardee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore, but EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore and margin fell to 10%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore on 17,645 MT sales volume, with PAT up 6% YoY to Rs 19.9 crore. EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore, with margin at 10% versus about 13% in FY26, attributed to higher domestic raw material and petroleum input costs and freight/supply-chain disruption linked to geopolitical issues. Installed capacity rose 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA effective 29 May 2026 via a brownfield debottlenecking of the existing refining unit (about Rs 15 crore capex). Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 10-20%, volume-driven, and EBITDA margin around 10%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 38,000 in Q4 FY26 and Rs 36,000 in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,167.7 crore / Rs 147.1 crore / Rs 84.7 crore
Long-term debt about Rs 20 crore (created 14 Aug); working capital limits almost unutilised; about Rs 150 crore FDR

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: 61.3% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management says domestic scrap procurement is costlier than imports and faces availability, pricing and GST issues from unorganised sources.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 38.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue; exports rose from about Rs 81.6 crore in FY24 to Rs 465 crore in FY26 across eight countries. Management says export margins are better after incentives and drawbacks, with working capital the same.

segments.name: Lead alloys
segments.commentary: Growing about 30-35% per management; ramp-up is slow due to OEM approvals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 10-20%, entirely volume-driven with no metal price contribution; volume target about 85,000 tons vs about 70,000 tons in FY26.
EBITDA margin guided at around 10% for the full year given the geopolitical situation; management said higher margins are possible only if conditions improve.
Plant utilisation expected to be below the 70-75% optimum range in FY27, with the full 70-75% level now expected to spill into FY28.
Working capital guided at 90-100 days; gross working capital requirement for FY27 above Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 220 crore funded from IPO proceeds.
Management expects return ratios to fall after the equity raise but to stay above 20% in coming years.
EBITDA per ton of about Rs 19,000 seen as fair if raw material costs stay at current levels; management expects a recovery to Rs 20,000-21,000 if the market normalises.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity raised 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA from 104,025 MTPA, effective 29 May 2026, via brownfield debottlenecking of refining capacity in the existing Naidupeta plant at about Rs 15 crore.
Management says the added capacity is a buffer and does not expect it to be fully used in FY27; current utilisation is about 65%.
Acquired and handed over a 5.56-acre land parcel at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, for medium- to long-term expansion.
No further expansion planned for now; exploring a mix of lead and other non-ferrous recycling for the new plant.
Company operates from a single facility in Andhra Pradesh and focuses on the southern market, exports, and Southeast Asia.
demand_pricing: Sales volume rose 13.6% YoY to 17,645 MT; management says the Q1 volume decline sequentially from Q4 was due to war-related import disruptions and deliberately measured procurement.
Realisation of about Rs 2,09,000 per MT on finished goods; management expects FY27 realisation to be broadly in line with Q1 but subject to metal prices.

Procurement: Middle East route blockages and higher trade and freight costs; the company is sourcing domestically via corporate tie-ups and auctions. Payment is made when goods arrive at Chennai port.
Customer concentration: largest customer down from about 70% to about 40% of revenue; top four to five customers account for most business.
Management says the LME listing of the Ardee 99.97 brand has generated more export inquiries; no specific new export orders were quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes fall sequentially, and what is the revenue potential of the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited war-related import disruption and deliberately measured procurement. The new capacity is the same facility's debottlenecking, with optimum utilisation at 70-75%; the company is currently at about 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-20% top-line guidance conservative and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative given trade and import/export uncertainty and would be happy to outperform; no FY28 numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 inventory build temporary and what is the cash impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was temporary and driven by OEM delivery timing at quarter-end; it varies quarter to quarter by customer need, and no cash impact figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 220 crore IPO working-capital allocation be used and what cash conversion cycle is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly for scrap buying from new sources and export credit to new customers. Working capital days are about 95 (110 earlier), expected to stay at 90-100 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and what is the post-IPO position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about Rs 20 crore taken on 14 August, working capital limit utilisation almost nil, and about Rs 150 crore in FDRs.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided for around 10% given geopolitical uncertainty, rather than the FY26 level of about 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation and implied FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 realisation was about Rs 2,09,000 per MT; an analyst's implied FY27 revenue of Rs 1,600-1,700 crore at 84,000 tons was described by management as a reasonable number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross profit and EBITDA per ton fall versus Q4 and Q1 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher costs for domestically procured raw material and petroleum-based inputs, plus freight and supply-chain disruption; management expects a recovery if the market improves.

risks_watch: Geopolitical disruption to Middle East shipping routes and import-based scrap procurement; management says it is not yet clear how the situation will pan out, and import share could fall if it does not improve.
Domestic scrap sourcing faces availability, pricing and GST issues from unorganised sources, and management says domestic prices are higher than imports.

Margin trajectory: Q1 EBITDA per ton fell to about Rs 19,000 from Rs 38,000 in Q4 FY26 gross profit per ton context; full-year margin guided at around 10%, with recovery to Rs 20,000-21,000 per ton contingent on market normalisation.
Utilisation: current about 65% versus 70-75% optimum; management expects FY27 below that range and the 70-75% level to spill into FY28, so the added 52,900 MTPA of capacity is a buffer for now.
Customer concentration: largest customer fell from about 70% to about 40% of revenue, but top four to five clients still account for most business.

Working capital: about 95 days now (110 earlier), guided at 90-100 days; FY27 gross working capital need above Rs 400 crore, with about Rs 220 crore from IPO proceeds. Watch cash conversion and the Q1 inventory build.
key_quotes: Right now, the overall market scenario with the whole war and being into import and export, so it is better to be conservative this year rather than say a number.

Basically, sceing the whole geopolitical scenario, which s not almost sceming to get over anytime soon, it would be better to for us to kind of say that 10% or 10% range would still be better for us to guide.
It is not necessary for us to consider that this whole 56,000 will be immediately used up.
Right now, once the new equity has come in, the return ratios will reduce. We believe we would be able to maintain 20-plus range in the coming years.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the structural recycled-lead opportunity, the LME listing and export margins, but cautious on FY27 guidance, which it repeatedly framed as conservative because of the war-related import and freight disruption. It was evasive on the exact FY27 and FY28 numbers, giving ranges and saying no exact figures would be provided.
